# dsh-agent-desktop
English | 简体中文

A DeepSeek Harness Host plugin that turns
`agent-desktop` — Vercel Labs' computer-use CLI —
into nat
ive `desktop_*` tools for the Harness agent.

`agent-desktop` reads and operates desktop applications through the OS accessibility tree: it
return

s a JSON snapshot with a stable `@ref` for every element an agent can act on, the agent acts
on a re

f, and snapshots again to verify. No pixel matching, no coordinates, the loop stays in the
agent. Th
is plugin gives that loop to DSH as first-class tools.

- Plugin release: `1.0.0`
- Compatibility: **DSH `>= 0.2.1-rc.5`**, tested with `0.2.1-rc.5` on macO

S 26.7.1 (arm64)
- CLI compatibility: `agent-desktop` `1.1.0` (JSON envelope `version: 2.6`)
## Why a plugin and not only a skill

The upstream project ships an agent skill (`SKILL.md`). DSH can install it as-is: its filesystem
ski

ll provider scans `~/.dsh/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`, parses the YAML frontmatter
(`name` + `des

cription`) and reloads the catalog without a restart. That is the right thing for
documentation.

There is one practical gap. The Harness **Bash tool is file-sandboxed**. On macOS the sandbox
cannot

execute `/bin/ps`, and `agent-desktop` builds its application inventory with `ps` for
`list-apps`,

every `--app <name>` filter, `launch` and `close-app`. Inside the Bash tool those
commands fail with

very `--app <name>` filter, `launch` and `close-app`. Inside the Bash tool those
commands fail with:

This plugin closes the gap by running the CLI from the **Host process** (no Bash sandbox), while
Bas

h commands stay confined. It also ships the skill's operating rules as a system-prompt section,
so t

he model knows the snapshot → act → verify loop, ref lifetime, retry dispositions and the
headless/h
eaded policy without a separate skill installation.
The skill and the plugin can coexist; they complement each other.

2. **Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`** (the Harness ships its own; nothing extra to install).

e executable if it is not on `PATH`.

Grant **Accessibility** to the app that launches the Harness (`DeepSeek Harness.app`) and,
if you wa
nt screenshots, **Screen Recording**. `desktop_status` reports both states.
## Install

The plugin is a local bundle: no build step, no install scripts, no runtime dependencies. The
`agent

-desktop` CLI and the macOS permission grant are prerequisites (see
Requirements); the steps below r
egister the bundle in one Harness profile.

nd adds its bundle row:

## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`index.js` declares `inject = ['tools', 'subprocess']`, resolves the executable lazily (PATH or
abso

lute), and registers one tool per CLI capability on the plugin context. Each call spawns
`agent-desk

top` with a collect-mode stdout/stderr, applies a deadline, aborts on tool cancellation,
and parses

the JSON envelope. Errors from spawning, timeouts and unparseable output are returned as
envelopes w
ith a `plugin` version marker so the model can tell them apart from CLI errors.

The CLI inherits the Host process identity, which is why the macOS Accessibility grant for
`DeepSeek
Harness.app` covers these calls.
## Security and privacy

- **Accessibility is powerful.** Granting it lets the Harness read and operate GUI apps. Grant it
on

ly if you intend to use computer-use.
- **Headless by default.** Ref actions use semantic accessibil

ity calls: no cursor movement, no
focus steal, no synthesized keys, no clipboard. Tools expose `head

ed: true`, which physically
drives input; use it only with explicit user permission. A headed action

may move the pointer.
- **Private data.** Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots and command outpu

t can contain private
desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads. The plugin does not

send anything over
the network; only the CLI runs locally.
- **Destructive actions.** `desktop_clic

k`/`desktop_type` can submit forms, delete content or send
messages. Prefer read-only observation fi

rst (`desktop_status`, `desktop_get`, `desktop_find`)
and treat irreversible actions as user-confirm

_status`, `desktop_get`, `desktop_find`)
and treat irreversible actions as user-confirmed decisions.
## Compatibility and verification notes

- Verified on macOS 26.7.1 (arm64) with DSH `0.2.1-rc.5` and `agent-desktop` `1.1.0` from the
live H

ost plugin: `desktop_status`, `desktop_list_windows` (271 windows),
`desktop_snapshot { window_id }`

(89 refs), `desktop_find { window_id, role, name }`,
`desktop_get`, `desktop_run { command: "focus"

ktop_find { app: "DeepSeek Harness" }` proves application-inventory targeting works from the
plugin

(it resolved the app and returned `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET` with both candidate windows, a `safe`
retry dis

position and a `--window-id` suggestion). On the same machine `desktop_list_apps`
returned `TIMEOUT`

twice: the global, unfiltered macOS application inventory did not stabilize
within 8 s or 25 s, whi

ch is a CLI-side inventory condition surfaced faithfully as an envelope,
not a plugin failure. Narro

w inventory calls (`--app`, `--window-id`) are unaffected.
- Windows and Linux are supported by the

CLI; this plugin is platform-neutral (it only spawns the
CLI), but runtime verification is macOS-onl

y so far.
- The plugin uses the Harness author-facing schema helpers (`defineTool`) and `schemastery

`, both
shipped with DSH; it declares them as peer dependencies and carries no bundled copy.
